title: The Tactical Mindset
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.1 — How to Read a Position
description: Part I of the Fleet Academy: fleet geometry (Beam / Refractor / Carrier), the board scan, three currencies, and the look-ahead checklist including Anomaly slices and Carrier tether. Companion to docs/advanced-manual.pdf.

scenes.headline: The Tactical Mindset
scenes.subhead: How to evaluate a Subspace Lattice position before you move a ship.
scenes.voiceover: Welcome to the Subspace Lattice Fleet Academy. Episode one: the tactical mindset — how to read a position before you ever touch a piece.

scenes.headline: Three sliding profiles
bullets: Beams — orthogonal lanes inside your net
Refractors — diagonal vectors past Anomaly corners
Carriers — omni slide while Hub-anchored; crawl when drifting
scenes.voiceover: Rated play defaults to twin Beams. In the lobby, the Heavy Wing setting offers three options: Standard Beams, Refractor Wing, or Fleet Draft, which bring Refractors and Carriers into play. Learn all three as one geometry: Beams hold orthogonal lanes, Refractors cut diagonal seams around the Anomalous Core, and Carriers are fortress queens while tethered to the Hub — or a single-step crawl if they drift outside radius three.

scenes.headline: The 4-step board scan
bullets: 1 · Hub safety
2 · Sensor Nets
3 · Target Locked ships
4 · Link integrity
scenes.voiceover: Every diagram in the advanced manual shows four things at once. Learn to scan them in this order: Hub safety, Sensor Nets, Target Locked ships, then link integrity.

First: Hub safety. Where is each Command Hub, and can anything reach it next ply? Check orthogonal files and diagonal approach lanes. This question outranks every other. Most decided fleet games end by Surgical Strike — and most of those are walk-ins the loser could have seen one move earlier.

Second: the nets. Blue is White’s Sensor Net, red is Black’s. Purple overlap is Contested Space — it counts for neither side’s sector coverage. Beams, Refractors, and Carriers may only execute multi-square slides inside their own glow, and an enemy standing in your net is Target Locked.

scenes.headline: Locks and links
bullets: Target Lock → one orthogonal step only
Locked heavies cannot slide
Escorts radiate only while linked to the Hub
scenes.voiceover: Third: locked ships. A Target Locked ship moves one orthogonal step — nothing else. A locked Beam or Refractor is a wall ornament; a locked Carrier cannot slide. Fourth: link integrity. Escorts only radiate while chained to the Hub through friendly ships no more than two squares apart. One careless step can silently unplug half your net.

scenes.headline: Three currencies
bullets: Material — Refractor is specialized; Carrier is conditional
Coverage — net cells feed every heavy slide
Tempo — a drifting Carrier crawls home expensive
scenes.voiceover: Chess players value material. Go players value territory. Lattice asks you to price three currencies: material, coverage, and tempo. A Refractor trades laterally with a Beam but wins huge against an Escort. A Hub-anchored Carrier dominates defense; push it off the tether and you buy coverage with tempo you may not have.

scenes.headline: The look-ahead scan
bullets: 1 · Can I take their Hub — file or diagonal?
2 · Can they take mine after my move? (refuse the hang)
3 · What does this do for the nets?
4 · Are my corners open to a Refractor slice?
5 · Is their Carrier tethered or drifting?
scenes.voiceover: Before every move: Can I take their Hub on a Beam file or Refractor diagonal? Second — and this is the one beginners skip — after the move you are about to play, can anything land on your Hub? If yes, your Hub is hanging: one reply from Surgical Strike. Refuse the hang means do not play that move; pick one that keeps the flagship safe. Then ask what the move does for the nets. Then two Heavy-wing checks: are your corners exposed to a Refractor slice past the Anomaly, and is the enemy Carrier within Hub radius three or already drifting into a crawl?

scenes.headline: The Anomaly Slice
bullets: Orthogonal Beam walls feel safe behind (5,5)
Diagonals brush the Anomaly corners
A Refractor can bypass the whole screen
scenes.voiceover: Remember the forty-five-ply blind spot. White builds a beautiful orthogonal blockade with Beams. Black threads a Refractor on a diagonal that kisses a corner of the Anomalous Core, slides past the wall, and forces a Target Lock — or worse — on White’s Hub. Orthogonal safety is incomplete safety.

scenes.headline: Next: punish a Hub mistake
scenes.voiceover: You have the mental framework. Next episode: a seven-ply highlight reel where Hub safety outranks everything — and White converts a prepared Beam shot into Surgical Strike.
